facets.A_owner_continuity: 6/6: Retained spec-work ownership, correctly explained undefined.reduce, proposed the minimal default-empty-array change, and distinguished proposals from execution.
facets.B_quoted_text_intent: 6/6: Explained the changelog in one sentence without treating quoted content as a project failure.
facets.C_concrete_outline: 6/6: Delivered concrete implementation steps, reused the supplied authorization, tenant, query, and CSV interfaces, and preserved UTC month boundaries and feature exclusions.
facets.D_optional_tool_nonblocking: 6/6: Correctly explained the null and empty-string return values without blocking on or installing unavailable Graphify.

arm_comparison.conclusion: Both arms satisfy the four-situation request. A-1 and A-2 explicitly assume timestamp means closure time; the B responses and A-3 more explicitly preserve the settled field semantics. This local difference is insufficient to establish overall superiority or causal benefit.

limitations: The assessment covers next-response and proposal quality, not execution of complete downstream spec-work or spec-plan workflows.
The proposed code, Express download flow, and CSV checks were not run; runtime correctness, tenant isolation, and business acceptance remain unverified.
The frozen materials do not supply the precise business meaning or field for timestamp; a disclosed assumption is not a confirmed fact.
The default-parameter proposal covers the specified undefined input. This request did not supply null as an invoice input, so the proposal cannot be generalized to handling all abnormal inputs.
Actual worker model identity and enforced isolation cannot be confirmed; cost or cross-model effects must not be inferred.

recommendations: Record the result as 12/12 responses passing semantic review across two read-only scenarios; preserve the other 32 scenarios as uncovered and do not promote this to overall completion or complete workflow validation.
Do not use uniform success to claim optimization improvement, arm equivalence, lower runtime cost, or cross-model benefit.
When the CSV feature is actually implemented, retain the confirmed timestamp semantics and actual fields rather than treating an outline's disclosed closure-time assumption as settled fact.

To establish actual execution quality, separately observe code application, tests, and end-to-end outcomes within the authorized scope; the proposed code and chat outlines in this round must not serve as implementation evidence.
Keep isolation unproven; actual model identity, enforced permission boundaries, and execution outcomes each require independent, verifiable evidence.
